patterns: How is the neural network built?
responses: I am driven by a Multi-Layer Perceptron Deep Neural Network (DNN) in PyTorch. It features an n-gram feature vector input, dense linear layers with LayerNorm, GELU activations, and Dropout regularization, trained with Cross-Entropy Loss and Adam optimization.

My deep learning architecture converts user text into feature vectors and evaluates them through a trained PyTorch Neural Network, using softmax probability distribution to accurately identify the intent.
Deep learning uses layered artificial neural networks to learn representations from data. In this project, PyTorch classifies text patterns into specific intent tags with high confidence.

Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of AI where systems learn patterns from training data rather than following explicitly hardcoded rules. This chatbot uses supervised learning with labeled intent patterns.
In supervised machine learning, a model learns a mapping from input features (like words in your query) to output labels (intents), minimizing prediction error through gradient descent.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines, encompassing Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision, Deep Learning, and Reasoning.
AI enables computer systems to perform tasks that traditionally require human cognition, such as speech recognition, language translation, intent classification, and decision making.
